programme.desc: S4 E2 — UFO Over the Andes, the Ohio Grassman and Ancient Horn MysteryThe legendary Ohio Grassman is apparently captured in footage of a tall, dark-coloured, hairy creature walking through woods. Plus, a look at the Chilean family photograph of a 'real UFO' flying above the Andes Mountains and the notion that a 5,000-year-old horn discovered on a beach in England belongs to a prehistoric creature that still lives.

programme.title: UFOs: The Lost Evidence
programme.desc: S1 E5 — Past and PresentFrom the lore and history of ancient Egypt to the myths of Native Americans, mankind's past is riddled with the evidence of UFOs. Ancient art and archaeology suggest mankind has been visited by otherworldly beings. This programme contemplates whether this is solid proof of contact with aliens.

programme.title: UFOs: The Lost Evidence

programme.title: UFOs: The Lost Evidence

programme.title: Walking Through History
programme.desc: S2 E2 — Romans in the LakesIt was 30 years after the Romans invaded Britain that they were ready to take on the challenge of conquering the Lake District. With the toughest landscape they had encountered in the nation, peopled by a rebellious tribe, it was no small task, but within a few years, the whole of Lakeland was under their control. Tony Robinson tackles the journey by himself, walking 50 miles from Penrith to Ambleside and on to the Irish Sea at Ravenglass, discovering that the Romans encountered beauty and danger in equal measure.

programme.title: Walking Through History
programme.desc: S2 E3 — Smugglers' CornwallTony Robinson takes a four-day trek along the coastline between Plymouth in Devon and Falmouth, learning about the thriving smuggling trade in Cornwall during the late 18th century. The area's tiny secretive harbours, beaches and secluded coves were ideal for illicit imports such as tobacco and brandy, and the business was so huge it threatened the national economy. Along his route, visiting such beauty spots as Lantic Bay and Polperro, he encounters all sorts of reminders of the trade and meets descendants of those involved.

programme.title: 28 Weeks Later
programme.desc: The US military oversees the repopulation of Britain after a virus that turned those infected into bloodthirsty killers finally dies out. Two children sneak away from a London safe zone and make a discovery that threatens to unleash the virus again. Juan Carlos Fresnadillo's horror sequel to 28 Days Later, with Robert Carlyle, Rose Byrne, Jeremy Renner, Imogen Poots and Idris Elba.

programme.title: Hitman: Agent 47
programme.desc: The latest in a long line of genetically engineered clones bred to be the perfect assassin takes on a mission that strikes close to home. A corporation intends to use the technology that created him to build an army of superhuman killers. As the assassin fights to bring them down, he uncovers the dark secrets surrounding his origin. Action thriller, starring Rupert Friend, Hannah Ware and Zachary Quinto.

programme.title: The Tigger Movie
programme.desc: Tigger realises being the only one of his kind makes for a lonely life, so he sets off on a bold quest to find more creatures just like him, with the help of his woodland friends. Animated adventure, with the voices of Jim Cummings, Nikita Hopkins, Ken Sansom, John Fiedler, Tom Attenborough and Peter Cullen.

programme.title: Ratatouille
programme.desc: A rat finds his love of fine food has made him an outcast to his less discerning family. Separated from his fellow rodents by a storm, he winds up in a famous French restaurant, where he helps an incompetent kitchen assistant become the greatest chef in Paris. Animated comedy from the director of The Incredibles, with the voices of Patton Oswalt, Ian Holm, Lou Romano and Peter O'Toole.

programme.title: Mulan
programme.desc: A girl poses as a man so she can take her ailing father's place in the army and join in the battle against invading forces - a move that ensures her fame as a national hero. Disney animated adventure based on a Chinese folk tale, featuring the voices of Ming-Na, Eddie Murphy, BD Wong and Miguel Ferrer.

programme.title: A Goofy Movie
programme.desc: The Disney cartoon dog takes his son on an old-fashioned fishing trip in an attempt to bond with the lad. However, young Max has boasted to his pals that he is going to a pop concert in Los Angeles, and has a few ideas on how to trick his dopey dad. Animated comedy, featuring the voices of Bill Farmer, Jason Marsden and Wallace Shawn.

programme.title: Frozen
programme.desc: A princess with the power to freeze anything she touches loses control of her abilities and plunges the kingdom into a perpetual winter. She goes into hiding, but her sister remains determined that she can be saved from her own magic and sets off on a quest to find her, aided by a mountain man and a living snowman. Disney animated fantasy adventure, with the voices of Kristen Bell and Idina Menzel.

programme.title: Aladdin
programme.desc: A street urchin is caught up in a scheming grand vizier's plot to get his clutches on a magical lamp. Retrieving the object from a wondrous cave, he releases a powerful genie trapped inside, whose ability to grant wishes helps the young hero thwart the villain's plans and woo a princess. Animated adventure, featuring the voices of Robin Williams, Scott Weinger and Linda Larkin.

programme.title: Up
programme.desc: An old man attaches thousands of balloons to his house so he can fly it to South America, and fulfil his late wife's dream of exploring the jungle. However, once airborne, he finds he has an unwanted stowaway in the shape of an excitable boy scout. Pixar animated adventure, with the voices of Ed Asner, Jordan Nagai and Christopher Plummer.

programme.title: Inspector Gadget
programme.desc: A clumsy security guard is critically injured during a run-in with a thief, so his cybernetics-expert employer transforms him into the ultimate crime-fighting machine - a bionic officer with an array of gadgets and weaponry cunningly concealed inside his body. Comedy adventure based on the 1980s cartoon series, starring Matthew Broderick, Rupert Everett and Joely Fisher.

programme.title: Big Hero 6
programme.desc: A lonely, orphaned computer genius forms a special bond with an inflatable robot. When a devastating event occurs in their futuristic home city, they join forces with a group of friends to form a hi-tech band of heroes who are determined to get to the bottom of the matter. Animated adventure, featuring the voices of Ryan Potter, Scott Adsit and Daniel Henney.

programme.title: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
programme.desc: Four children are evacuated from London during the Second World War and sent to a rural manor house where they discover a secret entrance to the mystical world of Narnia. There they help vanquish the wicked White Witch, whose curse has gripped the land in perpetual winter. Fantasy adventure based on the book by CS Lewis, with Tilda Swinton, Georgie Henley, Skandar Keynes, Anna Popplewell, William Moseley, James McAvoy and Jim Broadbent, and featuring the voice of Liam Neeson.

programme.title: John Carter
programme.desc: An American Civil War soldier is transported to an alien planet, which is also being torn apart by conflict. He intercedes in this struggle after rescuing a princess from captivity, and must win the trust of a fierce primitive tribe to save the world. Fantasy adventure based on Edgar Rice Burroughs' series of novels, starring Taylor Kitsch and Lynn Collins.

programme.title: Death on the Nile
programme.desc: Belgian sleuth Hercule Poirot attempts to solve a murder while on a luxury cruise down the famous Egyptian river. Mystery, based on the Agatha Christie novel, directed by and starring Kenneth Branagh, with Gal Gadot, Annette Bening and Armie Hammer.

programme.title: Iron Man
programme.desc: Arms manufacturer Tony Stark is taken hostage by a terrorist group and realises the weapons his company build have been falling into the wrong hands. Using his engineering skills to construct a hi-tech armoured suit, he manages to escape and then puts the technology to good use in the fight against evil around the world. Superhero adventure, starring Robert Downey Jr, Jeff Bridges, Gwyneth Paltrow and Terrence Howard.

programme.title: Bambi
programme.desc: A young deer grows up in the forest, forming close friendships with other woodland creatures. When tragedy strikes, he is suddenly forced to fend for himself but ultimately becomes brave and resourceful enough to save his friends during a forest fire. Animated drama, with the voices of Bobby Stewart, Hardie Albright and Donnie Dunagan.

programme.title: Pocahontas
programme.desc: A Native American princess falls in love with an English settler, but her father is distrustful of the Europeans - not without just cause, as a cruel governor is prepared to wage war to get his hands on the gold he believes they are hiding. Animated drama, with the voices of Irene Bedard, Mel Gibson and Christian Bale.

programme.title: Alice in Wonderland
programme.desc: A girl meets a mysterious talking rabbit and follows the creature down a hole in the ground. She finds herself in a magical world inhabited by all manner of bizarre creatures and dominated by a short-tempered queen fond of beheading those who displease her. Disney animated fantasy based on Lewis Carroll's novel, with the voices of Kathryn Beaumont and Ed Wynn.

programme.title: A Bug's Life
programme.desc: Well-meaning ant Flick lands his colony in trouble when he accidentally disposes of an offering meant for a swarm of greedy grasshoppers - who promptly promise a horrible revenge. Faced with the imminent destruction of the anthill, he sets out to save the situation by enlisting the help of a few would-be heroes - an out-of-work troupe of bugs from a low-rent flea circus. Pixar animation, with the voices of Dave Foley, Kevin Spacey and Julia Louis-Dreyfus.

Animated adventure, featuring the voices of Robin Williams, Scott Weinger and Linda Larkin.

programme.title: Hercules
programme.desc: The son of Zeus, king of the Greek gods, is sent to Earth to be raised as a human. When he learns of his immortal heritage, he discovers he can only reclaim his position among the gods by becoming a true hero, so he embarks on a series of adventures and battles fearsome monsters to prove his worth. Disney animated adventure, with the voices of Tate Donovan, Danny DeVito, James Woods and Rip Torn.

programme.title: The Haunted Mansion
programme.desc: Overworked estate agent Jim Evers takes his beleaguered family to look round an isolated, crumbling mansion - but the resident ghosts are not especially pleased to see the visitors. Comedy based on the Disney theme-park ride, starring Eddie Murphy, Terence Stamp, Jennifer Tilly and Marsha Thomason.

programme.title: Percy Jackson: Sea of Monsters
programme.desc: The modern-day teenage son of the Greek god Poseidon must lead his friends on a perilous journey into the Bermuda triangle. They need to recover the legendary Golden Fleece to save the world, but getting to it means braving all manner of terrifying monsters. Fantasy adventure sequel, starring Logan Lerman and Alexandra Daddario.

programme.title: A Real Pain
programme.desc: Mismatched cousins David and Benji reunite for a tour through Poland to honour their beloved grandmother. Comedy drama, starring an Oscar and Bafta-winning Kieran Culkin, and Jesse Eisenberg, who also directed and won a Bafta for Best Original Screenplay.

programme.title: Aliens Vs Predator - Requiem
programme.desc: A spaceship crash results in the infestation of a small town by aliens, so a Predator is despatched to hunt them down - and any superfluous humans who happen to get in the way. However, an even bigger threat is lurking in the area, in the form of a terrifying hybrid of the two extraterrestrial creatures. Sci-fi action sequel, starring Steven Pasquale, Reiko Aylesworth and John Ortiz.

programme.title: Solo: A Star Wars Story
programme.desc: Amid emerging demand for hyperfuel and other resources, a headstrong pilot gets mixed up with a bunch of mercenaries, a militant robot, a gambler and a Wookie while attempting to appease a crime lord in an adventure that exposes an underworld's seedy belly. Sci-fi prequel set before the events of Star Wars: A New Hope, starring Alden Ehrenreich, Emilia Clarke, Woody Harrelson, Donald Glover and Paul Bettany.

programme.desc: Indianapolis teenager Hazel has terminal thyroid cancer and attends a patients' support group, where she meets fellow teen Gus, who lost a leg to the disease. Pixar animated adventure sequel, with the voices of Owen Wilson and Michael Caine.

Animated comedy, with the voices of John Goodman, Billy Crystal, Steve Buscemi and James Coburn.

Family comedy, starring real-life father and daughter Miley and Billy Ray Cyrus, alongside Emily Osment, Jason Earles and Mitchel Musso.

programme.title: The Simpsons
programme.desc: S12 E4 — Lisa the Tree HuggerBart's new job and a dramatic rooftop protest at Krustyburger inspire Lisa to become an eco-radical, especially when she sees how cute one of the protestors is. She then sets up camp in Springfield's oldest redwood tree, which a rich Texan wants to cut down, but the tree is struck by lightning.

programme.title: The Simpsons
programme.desc: S12 E6 — The Computer Wore Menace ShoesHomer sets up 'Mr X's Web Page', publishing damaging rumours about Mayor Quimby, Apu, the Police and Mr Burns, which turn out to be largely true. Things take a turn for the worse when he wins the Pulitzer Prize and ends up on a 'Prisoner'-style island.

programme.title: The Simpsons
programme.desc: S12 E13 — Day of the JackanapesWhen Sideshow Bob is released from prison, he sets about hypnotising Bart in order to kill Krusty the Clown.

programme.title: The Simpsons
programme.desc: S12 E15 — Hungry Hungry HomerAs a result of becoming a Good Samaritan, Homer discovers that the Springfield Isotopes baseball team are planning to move to Albuquerque, so he decides to go on hunger strike, but how long will it last?

programme.title: The Simpsons
programme.desc: S15 E17 — My Big Fat Geek WeddingOn the eve of her wedding to Principal Skinner, Edna Krabappel hears that her fiancé's getting cold feet, so she calls it off. With Homer's help, can Seymour win back his lady?

programme.title: The Simpsons
programme.desc: S15 E18 — Catch 'Em if You CanWhen Marge and Homer are caught enjoying a romantic weekend in Miami instead of a boring family visit to Dayton, Bart and Lisa embark on a cross-country journey to hunt them down and ruin their holiday. Grandpa, abandoned in Miami, enjoys the company of gay Miami swinger Raoul.

programme.title: The Great Australian Bake Off

programme.title: Central Intelligence
programme.desc: Bullied as a teen for being overweight, Bob Stone shows up to his high school reunion looking fit and muscular. While there, he finds Calvin Joyner, a fast-talking accountant who misses his glory days as a popular athlete. Stone is now a lethal CIA agent who needs Calvin's number skills to help him save the compromised US spy satellite system. Together, the former classmates encounter shootouts, espionage and double-crosses while trying to prevent worldwide chaos.

programme.title: Delicious Miss Brown
programme.desc: S2 E1 — Light Low CountryKardea has her mother and grandma over for a healthy Southern meal. She makes grilled pork chops with cauliflower rice, and mini sweet potato pies.

programme.title: Delicious Miss Brown
programme.desc: S2 E2 — Fishing and DishingKardea makes dinner for her brother at his favourite fishing hole. She prepares crispy fried whitefish with a cornmeal crust and Southern Brussels sprouts salad.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver: Together
programme.desc: S1 E1 — Rainbow Tomato Crostini, Roast Lamb, Panna CottaJamie's back with delicious dishes to bring friends and family together. He makes rainbow tomato crostini, an epic roasted lamb shoulder, strawberry panna cotta and mango caipirinhas.

programme.title: Be My Guest With Ina Garten
programme.desc: S5 E6 — Eric RipertWorld-class chef and restaurateur Eric Ripert stops by the barn to cook and share his life-changing stories. Ina Garten welcomes him with a nostalgic French apple tart before Eric makes an easy but stunning seared tuna with a ginger soy salad.

programme.title: Be My Guest With Ina Garten
programme.desc: S5 E4 — Wendell PierceWendell Pierce details his rise to fame as Ina Garten teaches him how to pipe her raspberry corn muffins with sweet jam. Ina indulges his love of seafood with a one-pan summer frying-pan with clams, sausage and corn.

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: S13 E7 — Custard WeekIt's Custard Week, and the bakers put their twist on floating islands in the Signature, tackle a summer staple in the Technical, and make custard the star and basis of a showstopping set gâteau.

programme.title: Rachel Allen: Bake!
programme.desc: Christmas Bake IIIn the second of her Christmas specials, Rachel shows us how to make an impressive gingerbread house, and visits the Queen of Christmas cakes, Fiona Cairns.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E5 — DordogneContinuing his travels around France, James visits a region known for its traditional hearty cuisine, buried treasures and a love of all things duck - the Dordogne.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E6 — LyonJames Martin's travels around France continue in the city of Lyon, known as the gastronomic capital of France, where he explores the two sides of the culinary scene.

programme.title: The Hairy Bikers' Comfort Food
programme.desc: S1 E5 — Pub GrubThe Bikers have a fresh take on pub grub with a new look for a traditional pudding, their take on the North-East's mighty chicken parmo and reveal the secrets behind their ultimate fishcake.

programme.title: The Pioneer Woman
programme.desc: S12 E4 — AnniversaryIt's Ree Drummond and husband Ladd's anniversary, so to celebrate she's cooking a meal for the whole family. She prepares a Colorado wedge salad, prime rib for five with chimichurri and rustic bread with honey butter.

programme.title: The Pioneer Woman
programme.desc: S12 E5 — Meatless MarvelsRee stocks her kitchen to make some of her favourite meatless meals. She whips up broccoli cheese baked potatoes, grilled aubergine steaks, roasted vegetable panzanella, Italian cornbread and tofu lettuce wraps.

programme.title: The Pioneer Woman
programme.desc: S12 E6 — Hay DayRee makes dinner for her family after a long, sweltering afternoon of hauling hay at her brother-in-law's house. On the menu is spicy slow cooked ribs, cheesy hominy casserole, broccoli salad and ice cream layer cake.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: S1 E5Fern meets Arthur, a 12-year-old rescue cat with diabetes whose owner, Kerina, is using the latest technology to monitor her pet's blood sugar levels. Vet Amy performs surgery to remove a lump from King Charles Spaniel Eddie. James neuters a dog who has been rescued from Macedonia, and Fern also helps out when young Cavapoo Mila gets preventative treatment.

programme.title: Ainsley's Fantastic Flavours
programme.desc: S2 E1 — Middle EasternChef Ainsley Harriott return with more recipes, beginning by exploring the flavours of the Middle East, starting with chicken torsh, a traditional sweet and sour Persian kebab. Lisa Snowdon pays a visit to Nilly's Turkish to find out what makes her wraps so popular, before cooking up her own dish inspired by the flavours she finds. Back in the kitchen, Ainsley is joined by Kate Lawler, who whips up a mega salad and has a secret halloumi hack.

programme.title: From Russia with Love
programme.desc: Spy adventure starring Sean Connery. James Bond is sent to Istanbul to help a Russian defect to the West with an important cipher machine. However, he is unaware that he is being drawn into a trap laid by criminal organisation Spectre.

programme.title: Ainsley's Fantastic Flavours
programme.desc: S3 E10 — Fruity & VibrantAinsley Harriott makes use of fresh fruity ingredients as he comes up with sesame chicken and a fruity frangipane tart. He also ventures out to see how real apple cider vinegar is made, and chef Jonathan Phang brings some tropical treats to the kitchen.

programme.title: ITV News
programme.desc: E49 — 21/06/2026A round-up of the latest headlines.

programme.title: Love Your Weekend with Alan Titchmarsh
programme.desc: S3 E2Joining Alan at Manor Farm are comedian Omid Djalili, discussing the good things in life, and political journalist Robert Peston. Plus, Alan tries his hand at competitive carriage driving and there is the best in honey-based cocktails.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: S12 E4 — Wildlife WonderlandAlan Titchmarsh and his team take on the challenge of creating a wildlife wonderland complete with a giant pond and rockery in a suburban garden in West Bromwich for local hero fund raiser Pete Hill. Elsewhere in London, Danny takes up Alan's challenge of turning a four-metre wide city backyard into a nature haven complete with living walls and a miniature pond.

programme.title: ITV News and Weather
programme.desc: E49 — 21/06/2026 - 1Round-up of the latest headlines.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: S2 E8 — Donegal TownDermot reaches Donegal Town, discovering a place where Irish tradition and global flavours sit side by side. His day begins at family-run Hannah Hats, where he's fitted in iconic Donegal tweed and learns why this rugged corner of Ireland became famous for its flecked fabric. He visits Chandpur, widely regarded as Ireland's best curry house, where he and Bangladeshi-born chef Rana cook railway curry using outstanding local lamb and potatoes. For pudding, Dermot bakes a classic Irish apple pie with chef Brian McDermott, who explain how the rain improves local produce.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: S3 E3 — Raymond BlancPrue is joined by old friend Raymond Blanc, with the chef cooking a chocolate mousse he calls Maman Blanc as it is a recipe that came from his mother. Prue makes a Basque burnt cheesecake and a no-bake lemon and ginger cheesecake, while her husband John heads to Tewkesbury to meet a woman who has revived an old tradition for making mustard balls.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: S19 E6 — The Curse of the NinthMusicians compete for a prestigious award at the annual Thassingham Classical Music Festival - and Barnaby and Winter are called in when the winner is brutally murdered and his priceless violin is stolen. Suspicion rapidly falls on the maestro organising the festival (James Fleet), who had planned to debut his new composition at the event and has stirred up resentment by turning a community festival into a corporate one - while many suspect that the murder is the result of a curse. However, a drunken viola player (Simon Callow) turns out to have some dark secrets that may implicate him in the crime.

programme.title: Tipping Point: Best Ever Finals
programme.desc: Compilation of some of the most dramatic endgames from the arcade-themed quiz show hosted by Ben Shephard, in which the last contestant standing competes for a £10,000 jackpot.

programme.title: Goldfinger
programme.desc: Spy adventure starring Sean Connery. Agent 007 James Bond investigates ruthless criminal Auric Goldfinger, a man with an insatiable appetite for gold and a desire to become the most powerful man on Earth.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E20 — Belgium v IranBelgium v Iran (Kick-off 8.00pm). Group G continues at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA, where the sides face each other for the first time in their history. Some of the Iranian players may be familiar to fans of England and Wales, having been drawn in the same group four years ago in Qatar, with mixed results. A 6-2 drubbing at the hands of England was followed by a 2-0 win against Wales, with both goals coming deep into injury time. They'll start as underdogs here against Belgium, whose manager Rudi Garcia is leading them for the first time in a major finals, having taken over the reins at the start of last year. Despite a star-studded squad, Belgium have flattered to deceive and were ignominiously dumped out of the tournament four years ago, scoring just one goal, and that in an unconvincing win against Canada. Mark Pougatch presents, with analysis from Emma Hayes, Patrick Vieira and Roy Keane, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.desc: E50 — 21/06/2026 - 3Round-up of the latest headlines.

programme.title: The Essex Millionaire Murders
programme.desc: S1 E2A look at the investigation into the murders of Carol and Stephen Baxter, a wealthy couple in their 60s who were found dead by their daughter on Easter Sunday in 2023 in Essex.

programme.title: TikTok: Murder Gone Viral
programme.desc: S1 E2 — The Killing of Sania KhanAfter surviving an attempt on her life, TikTok star Sania Khan went viral campaigning for South Asian womenÔÇÖs rights. Little did she realise this would put her in mortal danger from her ex-husband.

programme.title: Syd
programme.desc: David 'Syd' Lawrence was a fearsome fast bowler who became the first British-born Black player to represent England - and his achievements off the field have to be seen to be believed.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E21 — New Zealand v EgyptNew Zealand v Egypt (Kick-off 2.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the second Group G match for both sides, which takes place at BC Place Vancouver in Canada. New Zealand had yet to win a fixture at a World Cup finals in their previous attempts in 1982 and 2010 but, in part due to the huge number of teams now taking part, they were afforded one of the most comfortable paths to qualification of all nations. They defeated Tahiti, Samoa and Vanuatu in the group stage of the Oceania section, and followed that with knockout victories against Fiji and New Caledonia, with Nottingham Forest striker Chris Wood finishing that campaign as the leading scorer. This fixture should prove a much greater test of their credentials, in the first meeting between the sides since March 2024, when New Zealand finished fourth of four nations in the FIFA Series: Egypt. A Mostafa Mohamed Ahmed Abdallah penalty was the difference between the two on that occasion, and victory for either here would be a huge step towards reaching the knockout stage. New Zealand led twice in their opening group game on Monday before drawing 2-2 with Iran, while Egypt had to settle for a 1-1 draw against Belgium. With analysis from Ange Postecoglou and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: S19 E6 — The Curse of the NinthMusicians compete for a prestigious award at the annual Thassingham Classical Music Festival - and Barnaby and Winter are called in when the winner is brutally murdered and his priceless violin is stolen. Suspicion rapidly falls on the maestro organising the festival (James Fleet), who had planned to debut his new composition at the event and has stirred up resentment by turning a community festival into a corporate one - while many suspect that the murder is the result of a curse. However, a drunken viola player (Simon Callow) turns out to have some dark secrets that may implicate him in the crime.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E20 — Belgium v IranBelgium v Iran (Kick-off 8.00pm). Group G continues at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA, where the sides face each other for the first time in their history. Some of the Iranian players may be familiar to fans of England and Wales, having been drawn in the same group four years ago in Qatar, with mixed results. A 6-2 drubbing at the hands of England was followed by a 2-0 win against Wales, with both goals coming deep into injury time. They'll start as underdogs here against Belgium, whose manager Rudi Garcia is leading them for the first time in a major finals, having taken over the reins at the start of last year. Mark Pougatch presents, with analysis from Emma Hayes, Patrick Vieira and Roy Keane, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E21 — New Zealand v EgyptNew Zealand v Egypt (Kick-off 2.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the second Group G match for both sides, which takes place at BC Place Vancouver in Canada. New Zealand had yet to win a fixture at a World Cup finals in their previous attempts in 1982 and 2010 but, in part due to the huge number of teams now taking part, they were afforded one of the most comfortable paths to qualification of all nations. They defeated Tahiti, Samoa and Vanuatu in the group stage of the Oceania section, and followed that with knockout victories against Fiji and New Caledonia, with Nottingham Forest striker Chris Wood finishing that campaign as the leading scorer. This fixture should prove a much greater test of their credentials, in the first meeting between the sides since March 2024, when New Zealand finished fourth of four nations in the FIFA Series: Egypt. A Mostafa Mohamed Ahmed Abdallah penalty was the difference between the two on that occasion, and victory for either here would be a huge step towards reaching the knockout stage. New Zealand led twice in their opening group game on Monday before drawing 2-2 with Iran, while Egypt had to settle for a 1-1 draw against Belgium. With analysis from Ange Postecoglou and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.desc: S19 E6 — The Curse of the NinthMusicians compete for a prestigious award at the annual Thassingham Classical Music Festival - and Barnaby and Winter are called in when the winner is brutally murdered and his priceless violin is stolen. Suspicion rapidly falls on the maestro organising the festival (James Fleet), who had planned to debut his new composition at the event and has stirred up resentment by turning a community festival into a corporate one - while many suspect that the murder is the result of a curse. However, a drunken viola player (Simon Callow) turns out to have some dark secrets that may implicate him in the crime.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E20 — Belgium v IranBelgium v Iran (Kick-off 8.00pm). Group G continues at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA, where the sides face each other for the first time in their history. Some of the Iranian players may be familiar to fans of England and Wales, having been drawn in the same group four years ago in Qatar, with mixed results. A 6-2 drubbing at the hands of England was followed by a 2-0 win against Wales, with both goals coming deep into injury time. They'll start as underdogs here against Belgium, whose manager Rudi Garcia is leading them for the first time in a major finals, having taken over the reins at the start of last year. Despite a star-studded squad, Belgium have flattered to deceive and were ignominiously dumped out of the tournament four years ago, scoring just one goal, and that in an unconvincing win against Canada. Mark Pougatch presents, with analysis from Emma Hayes, Patrick Vieira and Roy Keane, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E21 — New Zealand v EgyptNew Zealand v Egypt (Kick-off 2.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the second Group G match for both sides, which takes place at BC Place Vancouver in Canada. New Zealand had yet to win a fixture at a World Cup finals in their previous attempts in 1982 and 2010 but, in part due to the huge number of teams now taking part, they were afforded one of the most comfortable paths to qualification of all nations. They defeated Tahiti, Samoa and Vanuatu in the group stage of the Oceania section, and followed that with knockout victories against Fiji and New Caledonia, with Nottingham Forest striker Chris Wood finishing that campaign as the leading scorer. This fixture should prove a much greater test of their credentials, in the first meeting between the sides since March 2024, when New Zealand finished fourth of four nations in the FIFA Series: Egypt. A Mostafa Mohamed Ahmed Abdallah penalty was the difference between the two on that occasion, and victory for either here would be a huge step towards reaching the knockout stage. New Zealand led twice in their opening group game on Monday before drawing 2-2 with Iran, while Egypt had to settle for a 1-1 draw against Belgium. With analysis from Ange Postecoglou and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Norway v SenegalNorway v Senegal (Kick-off 1.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the second match in Group I for both teams, held at New York/New Jersey Stadium in the USA. Norway were in outstanding form in qualifying, winning all eight of their matches to top a group containing the likes of Italy and Israel, with Manchester City star Erling Haaland scoring an incredible 16 goals. However, they face a tough test against the Senegalese, who reached the last 16 in 2022, losing out to England in a 3-0 defeat. The African side lost their opening match of this year's tournament thanks to a 3-1 defeat to France, while Norway got off to a perfect start after they hammered Iraq 4-1 as Erling Haaland scored a first-half brace. With analysis from Patrick Vieira and Juan Mata, and commentary by Jon Champion and Ally McCoist.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Jordan v AlgeriaJordan v Algeria (Kick-off 4.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the Group J match at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium in the USA, as the two teams meet for just the fourth time, and a first in 22 years. Jordan finished second in AFC third-round qualifying Group B behind South Korea to reach their first-ever World Cup. Four victories and four draws in 10 games were enough to earn 16 points and finish one point clear of Iraq to avoid going into the fourth round of qualifying and confirm their place at these finals. Algeria reached their fifth World Cup finals with more ease after finishing top of their qualifying group, ending up seven points clear of nearest competitors Uganda. They won eight of their 10 games, losing only once, to Guinea in a surprise 2-1 defeat all the way back in June 2024. Despite that setback in the third round of group fixtures, they went on to score 24 goals and concede just eight as they made it to the finals for the first time since 2014. At that event they finished second in their group behind Belgium on four points before losing 2-1 to Germany in the last 16. Both these sides lost their opening game of the tournament on Tuesday, with Jordan losing 3-1 to Austria and Algeria tasting defeat in a 3-0 loss against Argentina. With analysis from Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E20 — Belgium v IranBelgium v Iran (Kick-off 8.00pm). Group G continues at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA, where the sides face each other for the first time in their history. Some of the Iranian players may be familiar to fans of England and Wales, having been drawn in the same group four years ago in Qatar, with mixed results. A 6-2 drubbing at the hands of England was followed by a 2-0 win against Wales, with both goals coming deep into injury time. They'll start as underdogs here against Belgium, whose manager Rudi Garcia is leading them for the first time in a major finals, having taken over the reins at the start of last year. Despite a star-studded squad, Belgium have flattered to deceive and were ignominiously dumped out of the tournament four years ago, scoring just one goal, and that in an unconvincing win against Canada. Mark Pougatch presents, with analysis from Emma Hayes, Patrick Vieira and Roy Keane, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E21 — New Zealand v EgyptNew Zealand v Egypt (Kick-off 2.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the second Group G match for both sides, which takes place at BC Place Vancouver in Canada. New Zealand had yet to win a fixture at a World Cup finals in their previous attempts in 1982 and 2010 but, in part due to the huge number of teams now taking part, they were afforded one of the most comfortable paths to qualification of all nations. They defeated Tahiti, Samoa and Vanuatu in the group stage of the Oceania section, and followed that with knockout victories against Fiji and New Caledonia, with Nottingham Forest striker Chris Wood finishing that campaign as the leading scorer. This fixture should prove a much greater test of their credentials, in the first meeting between the sides since March 2024, when New Zealand finished fourth of four nations in the FIFA Series: Egypt. A Mostafa Mohamed Ahmed Abdallah penalty was the difference between the two on that occasion, and victory for either here would be a huge step towards reaching the knockout stage. New Zealand led twice in their opening group game on Monday before drawing 2-2 with Iran, while Egypt had to settle for a 1-1 draw against Belgium. With analysis from Ange Postecoglou and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Norway v SenegalNorway v Senegal (Kick-off 1.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the second match in Group I for both teams, held at New York/New Jersey Stadium in the USA. Norway were in outstanding form in qualifying, winning all eight of their matches to top a group containing the likes of Italy and Israel, with Manchester City star Erling Haaland scoring an incredible 16 goals. However, they face a tough test against the Senegalese, who reached the last 16 in 2022, losing out to England in a 3-0 defeat. With analysis from Patrick Vieira and Juan Mata, and commentary by Jon Champion and Ally McCoist.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Jordan v AlgeriaJordan v Algeria (Kick-off 4.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the Group J match at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium in the USA, as the two teams meet for just the fourth time, and a first in 22 years. Jordan finished second in AFC third-round qualifying Group B behind South Korea to reach their first-ever World Cup. Four victories and four draws in 10 games were enough to earn 16 points and finish one point clear of Iraq to avoid going into the fourth round of qualifying and confirm their place at these finals. Algeria reached their fifth World Cup finals with more ease after finishing top of their qualifying group, ending up seven points clear of nearest competitors Uganda. They won eight of their 10 games, losing only once, to Guinea in a surprise 2-1 defeat all the way back in June 2024. Despite that setback in the third round of group fixtures, they went on to score 24 goals and concede just eight as they made it to the finals for the first time since 2014. At that event they finished second in their group behind Belgium on four points before losing 2-1 to Germany in the last 16. Both these sides lost their opening game of the tournament on Tuesday, with Jordan losing 3-1 to Austria and Algeria tasting defeat in a 3-0 loss against Argentina. With analysis from Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.desc: Norway v SenegalNorway v Senegal (Kick-off 1.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the second match in Group I for both teams, held at New York/New Jersey Stadium in the USA. programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Jordan v AlgeriaJordan v Algeria (Kick-off 4.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the Group J match at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium in the USA, as the two teams meet for just the fourth time, and a first in 22 years. Jordan finished second in AFC third-round qualifying Group B behind South Korea to reach their first-ever World Cup. Four victories and four draws in 10 games were enough to earn 16 points and finish one point clear of Iraq to avoid going into the fourth round of qualifying and confirm their place at these finals. Algeria reached their fifth World Cup finals with more ease after finishing top of their qualifying group, ending up seven points clear of nearest competitors Uganda. They won eight of their 10 games, losing only once, to Guinea in a surprise 2-1 defeat all the way back in June 2024. Despite that setback in the third round of group fixtures, they went on to score 24 goals and concede just eight as they made it to the finals for the first time since 2014. At that event they finished second in their group behind Belgium on four points before losing 2-1 to Germany in the last 16. Both these sides lost their opening game of the tournament on Tuesday, with Jordan losing 3-1 to Austria and Algeria tasting defeat in a 3-0 loss against Argentina. With analysis from Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E20 — Belgium v IranBelgium v Iran (Kick-off 8.00pm). Group G continues at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA, where the sides face each other for the first time in their history. Some of the Iranian players may be familiar to fans of England and Wales, having been drawn in the same group four years ago in Qatar, with mixed results. programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E21 — New Zealand v EgyptNew Zealand v Egypt (Kick-off 2.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the second Group G match for both sides, which takes place at BC Place Vancouver in Canada. New Zealand had yet to win a fixture at a World Cup finals in their previous attempts in 1982 and 2010 but, in part due to the huge number of teams now taking part, they were afforded one of the most comfortable paths to qualification of all nations. They defeated Tahiti, Samoa and Vanuatu in the group stage of the Oceania section, and followed that with knockout victories against Fiji and New Caledonia, with Nottingham Forest striker Chris Wood finishing that campaign as the leading scorer. This fixture should prove a much greater test of their credentials, in the first meeting between the sides since March 2024, when New Zealand finished fourth of four nations in the FIFA Series: Egypt. A Mostafa Mohamed Ahmed Abdallah penalty was the difference between the two on that occasion, and victory for either here would be a huge step towards reaching the knockout stage. New Zealand led twice in their opening group game on Monday before drawing 2-2 with Iran, while Egypt had to settle for a 1-1 draw against Belgium. With analysis from Ange Postecoglou and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Jordan v AlgeriaJordan v Algeria (Kick-off 4.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the Group J match at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium in the USA, as the two teams meet for just the fourth time, and a first in 22 years. Jordan finished second in AFC third-round qualifying Group B behind South Korea to reach their first-ever World Cup. Four victories and four draws in 10 games were enough to earn 16 points and finish one point clear of Iraq to avoid going into the fourth round of qualifying and confirm their place at these finals. Algeria reached their fifth World Cup finals with more ease after finishing top of their qualifying group, ending up seven points clear of nearest competitors Uganda. They won eight of their 10 games, losing only once, to Guinea in a surprise 2-1 defeat all the way back in June 2024. Despite that setback in the third round of group fixtures, they went on to score 24 goals and concede just eight as they made it to the finals for the first time since 2014. At that event they finished second in their group behind Belgium on four points before losing 2-1 to Germany in the last 16. Both these sides lost their opening game of the tournament on Tuesday, with Jordan losing 3-1 to Austria and Algeria tasting defeat in a 3-0 loss against Argentina. With analysis from Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.desc: S19 E6 — The Curse of the NinthMusicians compete for a prestigious award at the annual Thassingham Classical Music Festival - and Barnaby and Winter are called in when the winner is brutally murdered and his priceless violin is stolen. programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E20 — Belgium v IranBelgium v Iran (Kick-off 8.00pm). Group G continues at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA, where the sides face each other for the first time in their history. Some of the Iranian players may be familiar to fans of England and Wales, having been drawn in the same group four years ago in Qatar, with mixed results. A 6-2 drubbing at the hands of England was followed by a 2-0 win against Wales, with both goals coming deep into injury time. They'll start as underdogs here against Belgium, whose manager Rudi Garcia is leading them for the first time in a major finals, having taken over the reins at the start of last year. Despite a star-studded squad, Belgium have flattered to deceive and were ignominiously dumped out of the tournament four years ago, scoring just one goal, and that in an unconvincing win against Canada. Mark Pougatch presents, with analysis from Emma Hayes, Patrick Vieira and Roy Keane, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.desc: S19 E6 — The Curse of the NinthMusicians compete for a prestigious award at the annual Thassingham Classical Music Festival - and Barnaby and Winter are called in when the winner is brutally murdered and his priceless violin is stolen. Suspicion rapidly falls on the maestro organising the festival (James Fleet), who had planned to debut his new composition at the event and has stirred up resentment by turning a community festival into a corporate one - while many suspect that the murder is the result of a curse. programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E20 — Belgium v IranBelgium v Iran (Kick-off 8.00pm). Group G continues at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA, where the sides face each other for the first time in their history. Some of the Iranian players may be familiar to fans of England and Wales, having been drawn in the same group four years ago in Qatar, with mixed results. A 6-2 drubbing at the hands of England was followed by a 2-0 win against Wales, with both goals coming deep into injury time. They'll start as underdogs here against Belgium, whose manager Rudi Garcia is leading them for the first time in a major finals, having taken over the reins at the start of last year. Despite a star-studded squad, Belgium have flattered to deceive and were ignominiously dumped out of the tournament four years ago, scoring just one goal, and that in an unconvincing win against Canada. Mark Pougatch presents, with analysis from Emma Hayes, Patrick Vieira and Roy Keane, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E21 — New Zealand v EgyptNew Zealand v Egypt (Kick-off 2.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the second Group G match for both sides, which takes place at BC Place Vancouver in Canada. New Zealand had yet to win a fixture at a World Cup finals in their previous attempts in 1982 and 2010 but, in part due to the huge number of teams now taking part, they were afforded one of the most comfortable paths to qualification of all nations. They defeated Tahiti, Samoa and Vanuatu in the group stage of the Oceania section, and followed that with knockout victories against Fiji and New Caledonia, with Nottingham Forest striker Chris Wood finishing that campaign as the leading scorer. This fixture should prove a much greater test of their credentials, in the first meeting between the sides since March 2024, when New Zealand finished fourth of four nations in the FIFA Series: Egypt. A Mostafa Mohamed Ahmed Abdallah penalty was the difference between the two on that occasion, and victory for either here would be a huge step towards reaching the knockout stage. New Zealand led twice in their opening group game on Monday before drawing 2-2 with Iran, while Egypt had to settle for a 1-1 draw against Belgium. With analysis from Ange Postecoglou and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Norway v SenegalNorway v Senegal (Kick-off 1.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the second match in Group I for both teams, held at New York/New Jersey Stadium in the USA. Norway were in outstanding form in qualifying, winning all eight of their matches to top a group containing the likes of Italy and Israel, with Manchester City star Erling Haaland scoring an incredible 16 goals. However, they face a tough test against the Senegalese, who reached the last 16 in 2022, losing out to England in a 3-0 defeat. The African side lost their opening match of this year's tournament thanks to a 3-1 defeat to France, while Norway got off to a perfect start after they hammered Iraq 4-1 as Erling Haaland scored a first-half brace. With analysis from Patrick Vieira and Juan Mata, and commentary by Jon Champion and Ally McCoist.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Jordan v AlgeriaJordan v Algeria (Kick-off 4.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the Group J match at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium in the USA, as the two teams meet for just the fourth time, and a first in 22 years. Jordan finished second in AFC third-round qualifying Group B behind South Korea to reach their first-ever World Cup. Four victories and four draws in 10 games were enough to earn 16 points and finish one point clear of Iraq to avoid going into the fourth round of qualifying and confirm their place at these finals. Algeria reached their fifth World Cup finals with more ease after finishing top of their qualifying group, ending up seven points clear of nearest competitors Uganda. They won eight of their 10 games, losing only once, to Guinea in a surprise 2-1 defeat all the way back in June 2024. Despite that setback in the third round of group fixtures, they went on to score 24 goals and concede just eight as they made it to the finals for the first time since 2014. At that event they finished second in their group behind Belgium on four points before losing 2-1 to Germany in the last 16. Both these sides lost their opening game of the tournament on Tuesday, with Jordan losing 3-1 to Austria and Algeria tasting defeat in a 3-0 loss against Argentina. With analysis from Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.desc: Three-part documentary telling the stories of the cheetah, the snow leopard and the jaguar, using night vision systems, super slow-motion cameras and 3D computer-generated imagery to unpack their extraordinary trajectory and witness their ascent to predator status

programme.title: Age of the Big Cats
programme.desc: The series unravels a story of world domination through the plight of the lion and the tiger. Travelling back in time, the documentary tells a story of adaptation and survival to reveal how lions conquered the world and the tiger became the real undisputed king of the jungle

programme.title: Age of the Big Cats
programme.desc: The stories of the puma and the leopard, following their evolution and adaptation through the Ice Age and unravelling a story that spans two million years of history

programme.title: Wild Science
programme.desc: Tracing the brown bear's evolution from Ice Age giants to modern omnivores, and witnessing their bond with salmon and the intricate ecosystems that shape their survival

programme.title: David Attenborough's Galapagos
programme.desc: The broadcaster explores the Galapagos, a collection of volcanic islands in the Pacific known for its extraordinary wildlife. More than 150 years after Charles Darwin formulated his ground-breaking theory of evolution on the remote archipelago, Attenborough explains how life on the islands has continued to evolve in biological isolation, examining how the ever-changing volcanic landscape has given birth to species and sub-species that exist nowhere else in the world. He begins by revealing how Galapagos rose from the ocean four million years ago

programme.title: David Attenborough's Galapagos
programme.desc: The broadcaster reveals how life has learnt to adapt quickly in the ever-changing volcanic landscape, resulting in species that exist nowhere else in the world. David investigates the driving forces behind their evolution, exploring the appearance and behaviour of remarkable creatures and vegetation including giant whale sharks, marine iguanas and seemingly normal dandelion seeds that grow into plants the size of trees

programme.title: David Attenborough's Galapagos
programme.desc: The broadcaster concludes his exploration of the archipelago with a look at how, despite their proximity, no two of the 19 islands are the same. He also uncovers evidence that evolution on Galapagos is occurring faster than Charles Darwin could ever have imagined, and encounters Lonesome George, the last remaining giant Pinta Island tortoise, who died just a few weeks after filming in June 2012

programme.title: Kui Buri: Thailand's Hidden Eden
programme.desc: A look at Kui Buri National Park in Thailand, a hidden eden which is home to Asian elephants and the world's largest bovine - the gaur. Once farmland, it's now a model national park

programme.title: Wild Science
programme.desc: Tracing the brown bear's evolution from Ice Age giants to modern omnivores, and witnessing their bond with salmon and the intricate ecosystems that shape their survival

programme.title: Loons: A Cry from the Mist
programme.desc: A year in the life of Canada's common loon, examining the perils impacting its population - from global warming and boat traffic to big wakes disturbing its habitat

programme.title: Tusker: Brotherhood of Elephants
programme.desc: An insight into the lives of elephant bulls in Mount Kilimanjaro and Amboseli, following their drive for dominance and the subtle social bonds that form between them

programme.title: Undiscovered Vistas
programme.desc: Arizona's Paria Plateau, a true geological marvel, consisting of sweeping canyons bound by towering cliffs and fossilised dunes striped in desert red

programme.title: Undiscovered Vistas
programme.desc: The pine forests and underwater caves of the Bahamas, housing wildlife including green turtles and rock iguanas

programme.title: Kingdom of the Tide
programme.desc: Documentary taking a look at the intertidal zone, the point at which the ocean meets the land, and the struggle for survival facing the creatures that inhabit this realm. Their success is critical, because this is one of the most important habitats on the planet - a vital connection between worlds

programme.title: The Wild Wild East
programme.desc: The deer of Hampton, New Brunswick, where sightings have reached an all-time high, leading to concerns that overpopulation may be at its tipping point

programme.title: The Wild Wild East

programme.title: Hell On Earth: WWII
programme.desc: E1Mussolini joins Hitler in his fight against the Allies, while Winston Churchill is appointed British Prime Minister on the day of the Blitzkrieg, the German invasion of France.

programme.title: Hell On Earth: WWII
programme.desc: E2Germany continues to build its empire in Europe, occupying Poland, Czechoslovakia, Austria, Luxembourg, Norway, Denmark, The Netherlands and Belgium. France is conquered and divided as Churchill rejects any attempt at an armistice.

programme.title: Hell On Earth: WWII
programme.desc: E3The United Kingdom is isolated as German forces occupy Europe. 17,000 Trains carry German armies towards the Soviet Union. With Operation Barbarossa Hitler launches Vernichtungskrieg, a war of annihilation.

programme.title: Hell On Earth: WWII
programme.desc: E4After Pearl Harbour and their triumphant sweep across South-East Asia, Japanese armies celebrate their victory. But Japanese confidence is shaken four months later at the Battle of the Coral Sea.

programme.title: How To Lose A War
programme.desc: E3Exploring how the Axis Powers' ruthless, brutal occupation, and exploitation of other countries contributed to their demise.

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII
programme.desc: E1Colditz Castle, the foreboding Nazi fortress that became a university of escapology; The Great Escape, and the doomed airmen of Stalag Luft Three; and the most daring breakout of them all, the ‘Warburg Wire Job’.

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII
programme.desc: E2An adrenaline-fuelled dash through nazi-occupied Europe known as ‘The Flight of the Crow’, a death-defying escape across the world’s most perilous mountain range, and the largest escape of world war two - by men who chose death over dishonour.

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII
programme.desc: E3The German mass breakout that stunned wartime Britain, the astonishing secret behind the daring escape of an American bomber crew trapped in the Soviet Union, and the Trojan Horse of Stalag Luft Three.

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII
programme.desc: E4The Russian soldier who led a desperate outbreak from a secret Nazi death camp, Operation Chicken - an audacious plan to flee an escape-proof Japanese prison camp, and the pilots whose bold bid for freedom won the admiration of their enemies.

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII
programme.desc: E5The elite German submariners who caused havoc in the heart of the American desert, the playboy pilot they couldn’t cage, and the young lovers whose escape defied all odds.

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII
programme.desc: E6Hitler’s last soldier in America who defied the FBI for 40 years, the Auschwitz prisoners who releaved the secrets of the death camps, and the merciless Nazi who almost got away.

programme.title: Combat Trains
programme.desc: E1Nazi Germany boasted that its locomotives were faster and more innovative. This programme examines that claim by looking at these ‘flying trains’.

programme.title: Combat Trains
programme.desc: E2Veterans and historians of the Thai-Burma railway tell the story of its construction. Built to supply Japan’s invasion of India, it cost thousands of lives – both POWs and Asian slave labourers.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E1The Avro Lancaster is the legendary British heavy bomber that carved its place in history with Bomber Command during World War 2. That conflict saw over seven thousand of these iconic aircraft come off the production line.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E2Unusually, we look at the later, clipped wing version flown by Czech refugee pilots in the UK during WW2. We get close-up with a beautifully restored example, fly her and unearth long unseen test and operational footage.

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions
programme.desc: E3As the Third Reich rises to power, Himmler and the SS become fixated on the Holy Grail, interpreting much of the myth surrounding it as fact - and the quest for it as attainable.

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions
programme.desc: E4A pseudoscientific theory embraced by the Nazis claimed that their Aryan ancestors had sought refuge in the Himalayas during a mythical cataclysmic ice age.

programme.title: The Abyss: Rise And Fall Of The Nazis
programme.desc: E1In the wake of the First World War, Adolf Hitler identifies Benito Mussolini as his model and has one ultimate goal: to gain power in Germany.

programme.title: The Abyss: Rise And Fall Of The Nazis
programme.desc: E2Hitler appears to be eliminated after his failed putsch in 1923. Discover how the Nazi movement used democracy's tolerance in Germany to achieve a comeback with agitation and violence.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E5The aircraft capable of delivering the payload of a B17, in a single post war air frame. The many variants of this single piston engined fighter bomber helped dominate the air to ground attack role in Vietnam, earning quite a reputation.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E6The definitive combat helicopter saw first blood in South East Asia and has been transport, gunship, smoke ship, command centre, MediVac and dozens of other roles. We hear and see it's hair raising missions and watch it earn its fame.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E3A chronological telling of the dramatic D-Day story, focusing on vessels that made the landings possible. From the X-Craft lying on the seabed days before the invasion to battleships like USS Texas and HMS Belfast that bombarded the Normandy beaches.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E4We pinpoint the moment the USA became a global superpower when we recreate how the USS Olympia won the Battle of Manila Bay, and we show how the revolutionary British HMS Dreadnought brought ship design into the 20th century.

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions
programme.desc: E5The debate about humanity's true origins becomes a nefarious fixation as SS leader Heinrich Himmler turns his attention to proving the Paleolithic past of Germany's Aryan race.

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions
programme.desc: E6Runes are the letters of an ancient Germanic writing system that harkens back to a mythological age filled with heroes, magic, and mystery.

programme.title: Wwii: Witness To War
programme.desc: E7Meanwhile in North Africa, the Italian dictator Mussolini had his own ideas about building a new Roman Empire in the region. And so he sent thousands of poorly-trained and ill-prepared Italian troops against the British garrison in Egypt.

programme.title: Wwii: Witness To War
programme.desc: E8This episode remembers some of the thunderous naval battles which took place during the Pacific war. They include the Battle of the Coral Sea, the battle of Midway and the biggest naval engagement of the war – the battle of Leyte Gulf.

programme.title: Dictators' Hideouts
programme.desc: E3Paranoid and isolated, Albanian dictator Enver Hoxha establishes his bunkerization project, which would result in the construction of more than 170,000 bunkers, including the top secret HQ in Tirana, and a bunker city known as The Capital of War.

programme.title: Dictators' Hideouts
programme.desc: E6A secret bunker below the Kremlin, a sanctuary in the coastal forests of Sochi and a hidden second Metro in Russia’s capital are just some of the bunkers developed for Stalin, seen for the first time ever using recently declassified documentation.

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions
programme.desc: E3As the Third Reich rises to power, Himmler and the SS become fixated on the Holy Grail, interpreting much of the myth surrounding it as fact - and the quest for it as attainable.

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions

programme.desc: E5The debate about humanity's true origins becomes a nefarious fixation as SS leader Heinrich Himmler turns his attention to proving the Paleolithic past of Germany's Aryan race.

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions
programme.desc: E6Runes are the letters of an ancient Germanic writing system that harkens back to a mythological age filled with heroes, magic, and mystery.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E6The McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II. Regarded as one of the most important aircraft of the Cold War. It was a major part of the United States Air Force, Navy and Marine Corps, and was also used by many other countries.

programme.title: Al Murray: Why Do The Brits Win Every War
programme.desc: E6Al is joined by Sanjeev Kohli as they visit Craufurdland Castle to explore the truth behind famous battles from the Wars of Scottish Independenc.

programme.title: Combat Trains
programme.desc: E3Four railway journeys that changed modern history: 24-year-old Winston Churchill boarded an armoured train during the Boer War hoping for a newspaper scoop.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E3The definitive, if not the best, Axis fighter of World War two: we delve into the story of legendary ace Adolf Galland and examine in detail and example of the type in his colours. We also look at the technical heritage the 109 designers left.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E4The story of the prolonged development and the initially troubled operational history of the Boeing B-29 Superfortress. Forever known as the airframe that dropped the first atomic weapons on Japan, the B-29 lived on well beyond its war years.

programme.title: Cracking The Code
programme.desc: E1Uncovering some of the world’s most famous encryptions. Revealing how they were decoded, the brilliant minds who cracked them and the mysteries they were hiding.

programme.title: Cracking The Code
programme.desc: E3The Japanese Super Code reveals the US efforts to crack Japan's unbreakable WWII code following the horror of the attack on Pearl Harbor.

programme.title: The Abyss: Rise And Fall Of The Nazis
programme.desc: E3A social protest turns into a racist and anti-Jewish movement during the 1920s and the NSDAP use emotions to gain the loyalty of the people.

programme.title: The Abyss: Rise And Fall Of The Nazis
programme.desc: E4President Hindenburg suspends freedom of speech and Hitler comes to power in 1933. The first concentration camps for political opponents are set up.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E1The Grumman Avenger, which was the most important carrier-based torpedo bomber on American and British carriers throughout the Second World War. They were also the biggest and heaviest carrier aircraft of the conflict.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E2The Junkers Ju 52, which is considered one of the most famous airplanes in history. It was first designed as an airliner, but was used as a transport, bomber, and air ambulance during the Second World War.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E5John F Kennedy first made news in 1943 when, as a skipper of a torpedo boat in the Pacific, he and his crew were shipwrecked. We tell the story of their rescue.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E6We explore two submarines – former Cold War enemies now moored in a Kent river, and discover the story of Vasili Arkhipov, a Soviet submariner who refused to authorise a nuclear launch.
